Imagine…
in a single second, gravity doubles.
Everything on Earth becomes twice as heavy.
You are standing on a busy street.
Gravity pulls on you at nine point eight meters per second squared.
Now, it is nineteen point six.
Your ears pop.
The air at the ground would press down almost twice as hard.
If you weighed one hundred and sixty pounds, you would now weigh three hundred and twenty.
Your heart would have to pump blood that is twice as heavy up to your brain.
People stop.
Some sit down.
Cars sink on their springs.
Tires flatten.
Trees bend toward the ground.
Anything that falls would hit the ground about one point four times faster.
Balconies break off.
Windows crack in their frames.
A crane folds in half.
Buildings are designed with a safety margin.
But very few were built to carry twice their own weight.
The older towers give up first.
One floor onto the next.
Then, the dust begins to settle.
Much of the city is still standing.
Bent.
Holding on.
But from now on, every step you take would carry twice your weight.
